coverage.stoppingReason: Stopped after versioned mechanism and outcome evidence for the three required deep families and primary descriptions for the two mandated adjacent families; bounded time was reserved for both artifacts and validation. The report records the unresolved discovery queue.

eligibility.reason: USD-targeting fractional-reserve protocol launched and materially active in the window.

versions.label: FRAX v1 base fractional-algorithmic mechanism
versions.tokenRoles: FRAX is the USD-targeting liability; FXS is governance/value-accrual and the endogenous mint/burn absorption asset.
versions.backing: External collateral in approved pools plus the market value/dilution capacity of FXS for the uncollateralized fraction.
versions.redemption: At 100% CR, collateral; at fractional CR, collateral plus newly minted FXS; at 0% CR, FXS. Redemption and collection were split across calls.
versions.supplyPolicy: Minting burned/provided FXS for the algorithmic fraction; redemptions burned FRAX and minted FXS. Market price above/below $1 lowered/raised target CR at configured cadence.
versions.debtAndIncentives: Permissionless recollateralization rewarded external collateral with equal-value FXS plus 0.75%; excess collateral enabled FXS buyback.
versions.oracle: Uniswap TWAP market inputs plus Chainlink USD pricing according to v1 repository documentation.
versions.governanceAndAdmin: Owner/timelock and pool roles could configure oracles, pools, fees, ceilings and pauses; exact historical role holders were not reconstructed.
versions.liquidityDependencies: FXS market depth is essential to realize the endogenous redemption leg; collateral pools have ceilings and AMM liquidity affects exit execution.

incidents.summary: The v1 base mechanism was retired as Frax moved to later AMO and collateral-policy versions.
incidents.beneficiaries: FRAX users gained broader later stabilization machinery.
incidents.lossBearers: No specific loss allocation established by the cited retirement evidence.
incidents.outcome: Protocol continued; later mechanics must not be projected back onto v1.

eligibility.reason: Two separate chain deployments of a USD-targeting fractional-reserve mechanism were active in 2021.

lineage.relationship: Mechanism/code family described by contemporary analysis as Frax-like; exact fork commit unresolved.

versions.label: BSC IRON with STEEL
versions.tokenRoles: IRON is the USD-targeting liability; STEEL is the endogenous share/seigniorage token.
versions.backing: BUSD external collateral plus dynamically valued STEEL.
versions.redemption: Fractional redemption into BUSD and STEEL; exact contemporaneous parameter snapshot was not recovered.
versions.supplyPolicy: Mint/redeem arbitrage with dynamic collateral ratio.
versions.debtAndIncentives: STEEL farming/share incentives; exact emissions snapshot unresolved.
versions.oracle: Price/oracle design was functionally equivalent to Polygon according to the event study; exact BSC feeds unresolved.
versions.governanceAndAdmin: Iron Finance administered deployment; exact roles unresolved.
versions.liquidityDependencies: BUSD/IRON and STEEL market liquidity; deployment was not fungible or arbitrageable with Polygon IRON.

versions.label: Polygon IRON with TITAN
versions.tokenRoles: IRON is the USD-targeting liability; TITAN is the endogenous share/seigniorage and redemption token.
versions.backing: USDC external collateral plus dynamically valued TITAN; effective external collateral was about 75% during the run.
versions.redemption: IRON redemption returned USDC for the external fraction and newly minted TITAN for the balance, with TITAN valued by a ten-minute weighted average.
versions.supplyPolicy: Mint/redeem arbitrage; target CR could rise by 0.25 percentage points per hour.
versions.debtAndIncentives: TITAN emissions/farming and share-token upside supported demand but imposed dilution during redemptions.
versions.oracle: Ten-minute weighted-average TITAN valuation diverged sharply from spot during the collapse.
versions.governanceAndAdmin: Iron Finance could intervene with excess reserves; exact admin role map unresolved.
versions.liquidityDependencies: USDC/IRON and TITAN pools; redemption realization depended on TITAN spot depth and available USDC.

incidents.summary: Large TITAN sales after a price run-up made TWAP exceed spot; authorized mint/redeem paths overvalued TITAN, IRON broke peg, and slow CR adjustment could not catch up.
incidents.beneficiaries: Early/larger exiters and arbitrageurs able to transact against stale valuation.
incidents.lossBearers: TITAN holders through dilution/collapse, LPs through reserve composition, and late IRON holders through depleted liquidity and discount.
incidents.outcome: TITAN approached zero; IRON ultimately traded near residual USDC backing after transiently falling below it; reserve intervention failed.

incidents.summary: STEEL declined but BSC IRON did not break peg in the studied interval.
incidents.beneficiaries: BSC IRON holders retained contemporaneous peg liquidity.
incidents.outcome: Shows chain-local trigger/liquidity mattered; does not prove structural safety.

eligibility.reason: USD-targeting protocol-controlled-liquidity experiment launched in 2021, later redesigned and shut down.

versions.label: FEI v1 genesis/direct incentives
versions.tokenRoles: FEI is the USD-targeting token; TRIBE governs PCV and receives staking/IDO allocations.
versions.backing: ETH contributed through genesis/bonding curve became protocol-owned PCV, initially concentrated in protocol-owned FEI/ETH liquidity; it was not user-withdrawable collateral.
versions.redemption: At launch, ordinary holders exited through secondary markets; no general one-FEI-for-one-dollar withdrawal claim on PCV. Genesis token redemption meant claiming allocated FEI/TRIBE, not redeeming FEI for ETH.
versions.supplyPolicy: Bonding-curve issuance above peg; below peg, direct incentives minted buyer rewards and burned seller balances; PCV reweights could buy and burn FEI.
versions.debtAndIncentives: TRIBE liquidity mining; direct buyer reward/seller penalty. PCV absorbed market operations.
versions.oracle: Uniswap pool price and ETH/USD oracle inputs controlled direct incentives and reweights.
versions.governanceAndAdmin: TRIBE governance controlled PCV allocation and privileged minter/burner/PCV-controller roles; guardians could pause components.
versions.liquidityDependencies: Exit depended on AMM depth and composition; protocol ownership prevented core LP withdrawal but did not guarantee par redemption.

versions.label: FEI v2 reserve framework
versions.tokenRoles: FEI remained the USD liability; TRIBE served governance and a designed recapitalization/backstop role.
versions.backing: Diversified PCV tracked by collateralization oracles, with stabilizers and peg modules.
versions.redemption: Later stabilizers/PSMs provided more explicit reserve exchange paths than genesis; exact date-by-date caps are unresolved.
versions.supplyPolicy: Rate-limited minters, reserve stabilizer and peg modules replaced reliance on original direct incentives.
versions.debtAndIncentives: TRIBE backstop inflation below collateralization targets, paired with equity/buyback rationale.
versions.oracle: V2 collateralization oracle and resistant-balance components.
versions.governanceAndAdmin: DAO, optimistic timelock and contract-level admin/guardian roles.
versions.liquidityDependencies: Curve/Uniswap and diversified PCV; governance could allocate reserves and configure modules.

versions.label: Tribe DAO dissolution/redemption
versions.tokenRoles: FEI is redeemable against seeded DAI; TRIBE is residual claim token; eligible Fuse victims use separate capped claims.
versions.backing: DAI seeded for circulating FEI after protocol-owned FEI burn, plus residual asset basket for TRIBE and allocated FEI for Fuse claims.
versions.redemption: Immutable FEI/DAI 1:1 wrapper; capped Merkle exchange for eligible Fuse cTokens; pro-rata TRIBE redemption in listed assets.
versions.supplyPolicy: Wind-down burns protocol-owned FEI and ends active monetary development.
versions.debtAndIncentives: Shutdown establishes explicit seniority rather than ongoing incentives.
versions.governanceAndAdmin: DAO-authorized shutdown; dripper pause/rate limit guarded Merkle funding while primary wrapper was intended immutable.
versions.liquidityDependencies: Sufficient DAI seed for circulating FEI and funding of capped claimant contracts.

incidents.summary: Excess genesis supply sold below peg; direct sell penalties worsened practical exit and generic interfaces obscured them.
incidents.beneficiaries: Buyers able to acquire discounted FEI and recipients of configured buy incentives.
incidents.lossBearers: Sellers paid burn penalties and holders bore market discount.
incidents.outcome: Governance changed mechanics; later versions added explicit stabilization/redemption tools.

incidents.summary: A reported direct-incentive bypass could have repeatedly drained about 1,410 ETH; rewards were paused and a bounty paid.
incidents.beneficiaries: Reporter received bounty; no malicious exploiter established.
incidents.lossBearers: No exploit loss established; PCV/LP would have borne loss if exploited.
incidents.outcome: Temporary mitigation followed by permanent fix.

incidents.summary: Rari Fuse exploit produced losses after the merger; it was not the FEI launch peg mechanism failing.
incidents.lossBearers: Affected Fuse depositors and, through later allocation decisions, DAO residual stakeholders.
incidents.outcome: Separate capped claimant mechanism formed part of dissolution.

incidents.summary: DAO dissolution implemented separate FEI, Fuse-claimant and TRIBE redemption paths.
incidents.beneficiaries: Circulating FEI holders received a par DAI path; eligible Fuse claimants and TRIBE holders received designated distributions.
incidents.lossBearers: TRIBE was residual and claimant recovery was bounded by allocations.
incidents.outcome: Protocol ceased active development and redemption contracts remained.

protocols.name: Olympus DAO v1

eligibility.reason: Protocol-owned-liquidity/reserve-currency experiment active in 2021, but OHM had a floating target and no USD-par redemption promise.

protocols.targetUnit: Floating reserve currency; not a USD peg

versions.label: Olympus v1 bonds and rebasing
versions.tokenRoles: OHM is reserve currency; sOHM represents staked/rebasing exposure.
versions.backing: Treasury-owned reserve assets and OHM liquidity positions, including LP tokens acquired by bonds.
versions.redemption: No routine one-OHM-for-one-dollar redemption; exit through markets. Bonds exchanged assets/LP for vested discounted OHM.
versions.supplyPolicy: Treasury-authorized OHM minting funded bond payouts and staking rebases.
versions.debtAndIncentives: Discounted bonds acquired reserves/POL; high rebasing rewards encouraged staking.
versions.oracle: Legacy bond descriptions characterize market-driven pricing; exact v1 price-feed mix unresolved.
versions.governanceAndAdmin: DAO/policy roles controlled treasury, bond markets and minting.
versions.liquidityDependencies: Treasury-owned LP reduced mercenary withdrawal but LP valuation depended on both pool assets and market price.

eligibility.reason: Seigniorage monetary experiment active in 2021, but target was FTM rather than USD and there was no fractional external-collateral claim.

lineage.relationship: Project documentation names these as inspiration/predecessors.

versions.label: Tomb three-token seigniorage system
versions.tokenRoles: TOMB targets FTM; TSHARE receives expansion seigniorage/governance economics; TBOND is contraction debt.
versions.backing: No fixed external reserve claim; market demand, future seigniorage, liquidity pools, and a discretionary DAO fund support the target.
versions.redemption: Below peg users may exchange/burn TOMB for TBOND; above recovery thresholds TBOND may redeem for newly issued TOMB with premium.
versions.supplyPolicy: Above target epochs mint TOMB; below target, expansion stops and TBOND issuance contracts TOMB if users participate.
versions.debtAndIncentives: TSHARE LP farming and Masonry rewards; debt phase directs 65% of expansion to treasury for TBOND redemption.
versions.oracle: Six-hour epoch TWAP relative to FTM gates expansion/contraction.
versions.governanceAndAdmin: Developer-controlled DAO fund could buy below or sell above peg; exact multisig roles unresolved.
versions.liquidityDependencies: TOMB/FTM and TSHARE/FTM pools; voluntary TBOND demand and later expansion are necessary for contraction recovery.

incidents.summary: Project postmortem reports a malicious low-fee selling route promoted with false rug claims, followed by a run.
incidents.lossBearers: TOMB holders and LPs through price/liquidity stress.
incidents.outcome: Project continued after intervention; exact transaction-level causal reconstruction not completed.

claims.statement: A fast run can make fractional redemption reflexive because redemptions mint FXS whose sale reduces the realizable value of later endogenous redemption legs.

claims.reasoning: Causal inference from authorized token flows; analogous risk materialized in IRON but is not asserted as a FRAX incident.
